greeting: Atanirup atianik, Ataatap, Irniup, anirnialu Silapittiarup. Atanirup asannininga ilissinnut tamainnut pilik.
penitential: Ataniq, nalligijavuti. Kristusi, nalligijavuti. Ataniq, nalligijavuti.
psalm_response: The Lamb has made us a kingdom of priests to serve our God.
homily:
We begin today by looking at something very simple: a set of keys. In the first reading, John is weeping because no one is found worthy to open the scroll—the scroll that holds the history of the world, the meaning of our joys, and the secret of our sorrows. It is sealed with seven seals. It is closed. It is beyond human reach. And John weeps because he longs to know the truth of things; he longs to see the story make sense. How often have you sat in that same place? How often have you looked at the closed doors of your own life, at the questions that have no answers, at the silence that follows a prayer, and felt that same, deep, human ache? You want to know. You want the seal to be broken. You want to see the logic of the love that brought you here and the mystery of the departure that left you behind.

But then, the elder speaks to John: 'Do not weep. The lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has triumphed.' And John looks, and he does not see a lion. He sees a Lamb. A Lamb that seems to have been slain. This is the great, startling revelation of our faith. The One who holds the keys, the One who can open the scroll of our lives, is not the one who conquers by force. He is the one who conquered by giving Himself away. He is the Lamb. And because He was slain, He is the only one worthy to open the seals. He is the only one who knows the 'why' that we cannot find.

I want you to hold onto this image of the Lamb. It is an image of radical, defenseless love. Think of Benjamin. Think of his gentle spirit. Think of the way he looked at the world with such curiosity and kindness. He was a boy who understood, in his own young heart, the power of the open hand. Remember how he offered his entire piggy bank to his uncle? He didn't need to break it, he didn't need to smash it open; the offer was the thing. It was the movement of a heart that was already beginning to look like the Lamb’s. He was a boy who lived with his hands open, ready to give what he had to those he loved. That is the mark of a child of God. That is the mark of a soul that has already begun to live in the Kingdom.

But let us be honest about the ache. When Jesus draws near to Jerusalem in the Gospel, He stops. He looks at the city. And He weeps. He sees what they do not see. He sees the peace that is hidden from their eyes. He sees the coming storm. He does not turn away. He stands there, in the middle of the road, and He lets the grief of the world break over Him. If you are feeling that today—if you are feeling the weight of a world that feels like it is closing in, where the walls are being built up and the peace seems so very far away—know that you are standing with Jesus. He is not a distant God who watches from a throne. He is the God who stands at the gate of your city and weeps with you.

Alan and Thao, I know that for five months, you have been walking through a city that feels like it has been changed forever. You are carrying the memory of Benjamin, the brilliant boy who loved his 'Con Chim Airlines' and who listened to his father’s stories as if they were the most precious things on earth. You are carrying the silence of a house that used to be filled with his laughter. It is a heavy burden. But do not let your hearts be hardened by the weight of it. Do not let the grief convince you that you are alone. The Lamb who was slain is in the room with you. He is the one who knows the name of your son, and He is the one who is holding him in the light of the eternal day.

There is a temptation, when we are in the middle of such a deep sorrow, to wonder if we missed the time of our visitation. We look back, and we second-guess every decision, every moment, every breath. We wonder if we could have done more, if we could have seen more, if we could have protected more. But hear the truth of the Gospel: the visitation of God is not a test that you failed. It is a presence that you are living in, even now. You did not miss anything. You loved your son with a love that was a reflection of the Father’s own heart. You were the ones who gave him the world. You were the ones who traveled with him, who cheered for him on the badminton court, who shared the dream of the skies. That love was the 'visitation.' It was the presence of God in your home. That love is not gone. It is simply transformed.

Ryan, my dear brother, you are the keeper of the flame. You and Ben were a team. You knew the secrets, the jokes, the dreams of the future. That bond is not a thing of the past. It is a living, breathing reality. When you move forward, when you work hard, when you are kind to others, you are acting out the legacy of a brother who loved you. You are the one who knows how to keep the 'Con Chim Airlines' flying, not in the air, but in the way you live your life. Keep that curiosity. Keep that kindness. Keep that smile. You are never walking alone, because the love that bound you together is stronger than the distance that now separates you.

We must talk about the 'stones' that the Gospel mentions—the stones that will not be left one upon another. We often build our lives out of things we think will last: our plans, our ambitions, our sense of security. And when those things are shaken, we feel like we are being smashed to the ground. But the Gospel is inviting us to build on something else. It is inviting us to build on the Lamb. When everything else falls away, the Lamb remains. The love remains. The 'Well of Love' that you have established in his name—that is a stone that will never be moved. That is a work that will endure, because it is built on the mercy of God. Every time someone in a distant village drinks clean water because of the gift given in Benjamin’s name, he is alive. He is active. He is a part of the Kingdom that is being built here on earth.

I want to speak to those of you who are watching from afar, who are carrying a cross that you have told no one about. You are the ones who feel like the city of Jerusalem—encircled, hemmed in, tired. You are wondering if the peace of God is just a story. But listen to the Psalm: 'The Lord loves his people, and he adorns the lowly with victory.' Victory is not the absence of the cross. Victory is the ability to carry the cross with the love of the Lamb. It is the ability to keep standing, even when you are tired. It is the ability to keep hoping, even when the night is long. You are the lowly ones whom God is adorning with His grace. You are the ones He is calling to be a kingdom of priests, offering your own tears, your own prayers, your own lives as a sacrifice of praise.

Benjamin is now part of that great, heavenly assembly. He is one of those who is singing the new hymn before the throne. He is not suffering; he is singing. He is not limited by the things that limited him here; he is free. He is in the presence of the One who knows the ending of the story from the beginning. And he is waiting for you. He is waiting for the day when the scroll will be fully opened, when the seals will be removed, and when you will see him again, not in a dream, not in a memory, but face to face.

So, what do you carry out the door today? Carry the peace of the Lamb. When you wake up tomorrow, and the ache is there, do not run from it. Do not hide from it. Bring it to the Lamb. Tell Him, 'Lord, I am here. I am tired. But I am Yours.' And then, do one small thing in Benjamin’s name. A kind word to a stranger, a moment of patience in traffic, a prayer for someone who is struggling—let the love that he shared continue to flow through you. You are the hands and the heart of God in this world. You are the ones who make the love of the Lamb visible to those who are lost. You are not alone. You are held. You are loved. And you are being led, step by step, toward the banquet where there are no more tears, no more goodbyes, and no more closed doors. Only the light of the Lamb, and the joy of being home. Amen.
spiritual_communion: My Jesus, I believe that You are present in the Most Holy Sacrament. I love You above all things, and I desire to receive You into my soul. Since I cannot at this moment receive You sacramentally, come at least spiritually into my heart. I embrace You as if You were already there and unite myself wholly to You. Never permit me to be separated from You. Amen.
closing: May the Lord bless you and keep you, and may the light of His face shine upon you and give you peace. Amen.
standing_petitions: For Benjamin and all who have gone before us, that they may rest in the eternal light of Christ’s presence.
For all who grieve, that the Lord may console them with His peace and grant them the hope of the resurrection.

readings.label: Reading 1
readings.text: I, John, saw a scroll in the right hand of the one who sat on the throne. It had writing on both sides and was sealed with seven seals. Then I saw a mighty angel who proclaimed in a loud voice, 'Who is worthy to open the scroll and break its seals?' But no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or to examine it. I shed many tears because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or to examine it. One of the elders said to me, 'Do not weep. The lion of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, has triumphed, enabling him to open the scroll with its seven seals.' Then I saw standing in the midst of the throne and the four living creatures and the elders a Lamb that seemed to have been slain. He had seven horns and seven eyes; these are the seven spirits of God sent out into the whole world. He came and received the scroll from the right hand of the one who sat on the throne. When he took it, the four living creatures and the twenty-four elders fell down before the Lamb. Each of the elders held a harp and gold bowls filled with incense, which are the prayers of the holy ones. They sang a new hymn: 'Worthy are you to receive the scroll and break open its seals, for you were slain and with your Blood you purchased for God those from every tribe and tongue, people and nation. You made them a kingdom and priests for our God, and they will reign on earth.'

readings.label: Gospel
readings.text: As Jesus drew near Jerusalem, he saw the city and wept over it, saying, 'If this day you only knew what makes for peace– but now it is hidden from your eyes. For the days are coming upon you when your enemies will raise a palisade against you; they will encircle you and hem you in on all sides. They will smash you to the ground and your children within you, and they will not leave one stone upon another within you because you did not recognize the time of your visitation.'

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: I miss you so much Ben! Ba má nhớ con rất nhiều mỗi ngày.
Nha Trang, ngày 31/10/2026, anh Minh suy nghĩ về Ben rất nhiều. Nhớ và thương em!!!

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - mom and I have been missing you a lot.   Saw you a few times in my dreams last few weeks! Come and say hi daily okay?
Thinking of you buddy! Stop by to say hello whenever you can okay? Love you Ben

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Hey Ben - Been dreaming about you a lot. Hope you're having fun up in heaven. Please look after our family. Remember to come say hi daily. We miss you so much!

Ben ơi, trong giấc ngủ anh Huy đã thấy Ben về thăm anh, trao cho anh lời cầu nguyện để hai anh em mình lại được tìm thấy nhau. Xin Chúa thương nhậm lời Ben, cho Ben được hưởng ngàn thu bình an bên Chúa. Nếu có thể, xin Ben lại ghé thăm anh trong những giấc mơ tiếp theo nhé, dù chỉ là một lời chào hay một nụ cười thân thương như ngày nào.

pet_prayers.name: Dad
pet_prayers.text: Ben, my sweet boy, I miss you so much. Thank you for visiting me and Chú Chris last night. He told me he saw you flying a helicopter—so free, joyful, and strong up there. Down here, Mom and I are crying more and more each day. A piece of my heart feels completely dead without you, Ben. Please watch over us, pray for your mom, your brother Ryan, and me, and give us the strength to keep going. We love you forever
